purpose: Candidate retrieval, scoped feature lookup, and concept-graph membership. LLM review decides identity and applicability.

object.definition: $$\mathcal A=\{a\in\mathbb R^d:\|a\|_p\le1\},\qquad 1<p\le2,\qquad q=\frac{p}{p-1}.$$ $$\theta_t\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\sim\nu,\qquad \mathbb E\theta_t=\theta_*,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\theta_t)=\Sigma,\qquad |\langle a,\theta_t\rangle|\le1\quad\text{almost surely, for every }a\in\mathcal A.$$ Randomness comes from a fresh parameter vector each round; the feedback is not a linear regression observation with additive homoscedastic scalar noise. $$N=T,\qquad \sigma_q^2=\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}\Sigma_{ii}^{q/2}\right)^{2/q}.$$ Here $N$ counts scalar observations. The quantity $\sigma_q^2$ is defined by the covariance diagonal and cannot be replaced by the maximum action variance.

operation.query_signature: $$Y_t=\langle a_t,\theta_t\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(Y_t\mid a_t)=a_t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma a_t.$$ Choose $a_t$ first, then draw a fresh $\theta_t$ and reveal only the scalar projection. The same $\theta_t$ defines all counterfactual rewards that round, but other projections are hidden. Causal policies are allowed. Inputs $d,p,q,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ are public; the distribution $\nu$, mean $\theta_*$, and covariance $\Sigma$ are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available. Within-round exceptions require explicit full-function or common-sample access.

protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
steps: The algorithm chooses $a_t$ before a fresh $\theta_t$ is drawn and observes only one scalar projection. The same $\theta_t$ defines rewards for all counterfactual actions that round, but the other projections remain hidden.
Causal strategies are allowed. The quantity $d,p,q,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ is public.
The distribution $\nu$, mean parameter $\theta_*$, and covariance matrix $\Sigma$ are all hidden.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
